items.followUp: When does an electron absorb energy according to Bohr’s model?

rubric.why: The student identifies the transition during which the electron loses energy.
rubric.description: States that an electron emits energy when it moves from a higher-energy orbit to a lower-energy orbit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction of the transition and emission of energy.

rubric.why: The student identifies the transition during which the electron gains energy.
rubric.description: States that an electron absorbs energy when it moves from a lower-energy orbit to a higher-energy orbit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction of the transition and absorption of energy.

modelAnswer: An electron emits energy when it jumps from a higher-energy orbit to a lower-energy orbit.
It absorbs energy when it jumps from a lower-energy orbit to a higher-energy orbit.

items.followUp: Define ionization energy and give one example of an atom forming a positive ion.

rubric.why: The definition must state what happens when an electron is added to an atom.
rubric.description: Defines electron affinity as the energy released when a gaseous atom accepts an electron to form a negative ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the electron gain and formation of a negative ion; include energy release for full credit on this point.

rubric.why: A correct example shows electron affinity in a specific atom.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example, such as a chlorine atom accepting an electron to form a chloride ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example and product.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity is the energy released when a neutral gaseous atom accepts an electron to form a negative ion.
For example: Cl(g) + e⁻ → Cl⁻(g) + energy.

items.followUp: Define a group and a period in the modern periodic table.

rubric.why: A group is identified by its vertical arrangement in the table.
rubric.description: Defines a group as a vertical column of elements in the modern periodic table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a group as a vertical column.

rubric.why: A period is identified by its horizontal arrangement in the table.
rubric.description: Defines a period as a horizontal row of elements in the modern periodic table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a period as a horizontal row.

modelAnswer: A group is a vertical column of elements in the modern periodic table.
A period is a horizontal row of elements in the modern periodic table.

items.followUp: Describe how atomic radius changes across a period and down a group.

rubric.why: This is the periodic trend in atomic radius within a group.
rubric.description: States that atomic radius increases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct trend down a group.

rubric.why: This is the periodic trend in atomic radius across a period.
rubric.description: States that atomic radius decreases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct trend across a period.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius increases down a group.
Atomic radius decreases from left to right across a period.

items.followUp: How many elements are present in the 1st and 4th periods of the modern periodic table?

rubric.why: The second period contains eight elements.
rubric.description: Gives the number of elements in the second period as 8.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct count.

rubric.why: The third period contains eight elements.
rubric.description: Gives the number of elements in the third period as 8.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct count.

items.followUp: What is diffusion in gases? Give an example involving two gases.

rubric.why: The definition should describe the spreading and mixing of gas particles.
rubric.description: Defines diffusion of gases as the spontaneous spreading and mixing of gas particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct description of gas particles spreading or mixing.

rubric.why: A specific example demonstrates diffusion of gases.
rubric.description: Gives the example of ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases diffusing and forming ammonium chloride.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example involving gases.

modelAnswer: Diffusion of gases is the spontaneous spreading and mixing of gas particles.
For example, ammonia gas and hydrogen chloride gas diffuse towards each other and form a white ring of ammonium chloride.

rubric.why: Silver is commonly used to make decorative articles.
rubric.description: Names jewellery or ornaments as a use of silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid use of silver.

rubric.why: Silver has other recognised practical uses besides decorative articles.
rubric.description: Names photography, silvering mirrors, or making coins as another use of silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one further valid use of silver.

modelAnswer: Silver is used to make jewellery and ornaments.
It is also used in photography and for silvering mirrors.

items.followUp: Why does the reactivity of alkali metals increase down Group 1?

rubric.why: Increasing atomic size places the outer electron farther from the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that atomic radius increases down the group, so the outer electron is farther from the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the increasing atomic size or distance of the outer electron.

rubric.why: The outer electron becomes easier to remove, increasing metallic reactivity.
rubric.description: Explains that weaker attraction or lower ionization energy makes the outer electron easier to lose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking easier loss of the outer electron to increased reactivity.

modelAnswer: Down a group, atomic radius increases and the outermost electron is farther from the nucleus.
The attraction between the nucleus and this electron decreases, so the electron is lost more easily and the metal becomes more reactive.
